details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

TCP established ehash lookups are lockless. The socket caches involved
use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU, so memory can be reused before an RCU reader
that retained its old address has finished.

After a tuple match, __inet_lookup_established() and
__inet6_lookup_established() acquire a reference and repeat the tuple
check. They do not check whether the new object is hashed. If the
address is reused for a socket with the same tuple, the lookup can
acquire a reference to the new object and return it while its nulls node
is unhashed.

A PoC that drives reuse with a SYN cookie request socket reproduced the
crash. The new request socket is unhashed and has a NULL rsk_listener.
A lookup that had loaded the address of the old request socket acquired
the reference published by tcp_get_cookie_sock() and returned the new
object. tcp_v4_rcv() then read sk_state through the NULL listener.

The resulting crash was:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000012
  #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
  ...
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 4 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/4 Not tainted 7.3.0-00591-g0e135910deec #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  ...
  RIP: 0010:tcp_v4_rcv+0x44e/0x1280
  ...
  R10: 0000000000000001 R11: 00000000024ca8c0 R12: 0000000000000000
  ...
  CR2: 0000000000000012 CR3: 0000000103d50004 CR4: 0000000000770ef0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   ? raw_local_deliver+0xae/0x240
   ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x2d/0x180
   ip_local_deliver_finish+0x84/0x100
   ip_sublist_rcv_finish+0x5f/0x70
   ip_sublist_rcv+0x12a/0x1d0
   ip_list_rcv+0xfd/0x130
   __netif_receive_skb_list_core+0x223/0x250
   netif_receive_skb_list_internal+0x1d2/0x2c0
   ? try_fill_recv+0x39/0x7b0
   napi_complete_done+0x74/0x170
   virtnet_poll+0x445/0x600
   __napi_poll+0x27/0x1e0
   net_rx_action+0x2fe/0x3b0
   handle_softirqs+0xc2/0x2c0
   __irq_exit_rcu+0x74/0xd0
   common_interrupt+0x7f/0x90
   </IRQ>
  ...
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

After taking a reference, check whether the nulls node is unhashed in
both IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups. If it is unhashed or the tuple
no longer matches, drop the reference and restart the lookup.

Lookups racing with the TIME_WAIT hashdance, or with a request being
replaced by its child, now restart and find the new socket instead of
returning the old one.

Request sockets that were never inserted into ehash can have a nonzero
refcount, and a stale lookup can hold a transient reference. Therefore,
when SYN cookie, Fast Open, and request migration paths fail after
setting a nonzero refcount, release the references held by those paths
with reqsk_put() instead of freeing the request directly.

Qbian61 forum-java commit 20f7e68 through commit 63152c4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by posting unsanitized comment content rendered via jQuery .html() in the reply dialog. Attackers can post comments with img onerror payloads that execute when victims click Reply, stealing the non-HttpOnly sid session cookie to hijack accounts including administrators.

# Missing validation of CONNECT requests in http2

For CONNECT requests, `checkRequestHeader` (`Network/HTTP2/H2/HPACK.hs`) in http2 up to 5.4.13 returned early, only requiring the absence of `:scheme` and `:path`. Every other check was skipped:

* the requirement that `:authority` is present (RFC 9113, Section 8.5);
* the check that `:authority` and `Host` agree, which applies to every other request (RFC 9113, Section 8.3.1: a server SHOULD treat a mismatch as malformed);
* the common checks for `:status`, `Connection` and `TE`.

A CONNECT request carrying `:authority: a.example` and `Host: b.example` was therefore accepted. Consumers that read `Host` see `b.example` where intermediaries that read `:authority` see `a.example`. warp, for example, sets `requestHeaderHost` to `Host` when present and falls back to `:authority`, so an application behind an intermediary that routes or authorizes on `:authority` handles a request other than the one the intermediary validated — a request can be smuggled past the front-end's access control, validation, logging or WAF rules.

Exploitation requires a front-end that makes decisions based on `:authority` while the application behind it bases routing or authorization on `Host`; a directly exposed server sees only one authority.

A CONNECT request with neither `:authority` nor `:path` also passed validation and reached warp 3.4.21, where `fromJust (mPath <|> mAuth)` (`Network/Wai/Handler/Warp/HTTP2/Request.hs`) threw. The exception was raised in the stream's worker thread, so it reset one stream and did not affect the server process.

## Resolution

http2 5.4.14 validates CONNECT requests like every other request: `:authority` is required, `:scheme` and `:path` are forbidden, and the common checks apply, including the `:authority`/`Host` consistency check. A malformed request is rejected with a stream error of type `PROTOCOL_ERROR`, leaving the connection itself in place. With every request thus carrying `:path` or `:authority` when it reaches warp, the `fromJust` can no longer fail, so warp needs no change.

The same release also stops the server from pushing on a request that has no `:scheme` or `:authority`, where a push previously crashed on the missing `:scheme`.

Upgrade to http2 5.4.14 or later. Series before 4.0 performed no `:authority`/`Host` consistency check at all, for any request, and are unsupported; upgrade regardless.

## Credits

Reported by Akash Sebastian (@akashseb). Validated and fixed by Kazu Yamamoto.

details:
Sandboxed and extendable image decoding.

Security Fix(es):

* librsvg: Use-after-free when XML includes have duplicated entities (CVE-2026-96889,RUSTSEC-2026-0305)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

The glib-networking packages provide modules that extend the networking support in Glib. In particular, the packages contain a libproxy-based implementation of the GProxyResolver class type and a gnutls-based implementation of the GTlsConnection class type.

Security Fix(es):

* glib-networking: Unbounded TLS 1.3 session ticket queue growth in glib-networking allows remote denial of service (CVE-2026-103963)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

The environment-modules packages provide dynamic modification of user environment using module files. Each module file contains the information needed to configure the shell for an application. Once the package is initialized, the environment can be modified on a per-module basis using the "module" utility, which interprets module files.

Security Fix(es):

* environment-modules: Command injection in environment-modules Bash completion via malicious module names containing shell metacharacters (CVE-2026-85013)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.
